papers.title: Mucinase-engineered cell membrane nanovesicles degrade the glycocalyx shield to potentiate antitumor immunity
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: The tumor glycocalyx forms a protective shield that masks checkpoint proteins and compromises the efficacy of immunotherapies. While the bacterial protease StcE can degrade this barrier by cleaving O-glycosylated mucin domains, its therapeutic potential is hindered by off-target toxicity and high immunogenicity. To overcome these limitations, we developed a biomimetic platform of cell membrane fusion nanovesicles (FNVs) that codisplay StcE and CD47 nanobodies (nCD47) for spatially controlled glycocalyx degradation and enhanced checkpoint blockade. Using the SpyTag/SpyCatcher system, we generated StcE-displaying NVs, which were then fused with nCD47-displaying NVs. The resulting StcE-nCD47-FNVs retained potent mucin-hydrolyzing activity and exhibited well-defined physicochemical properties. By removing the mucin barrier, StcE-nCD47-FNVs significantly enhanced nCD47 binding to CD47 on tumor cells, thereby potentiating antitumor immune responses. More importantly, benefiting from prolonged circulation of FNVs and tumor targeting of nCD47, the StcE-nCD47-FNV platform demonstrated superior tumor accumulation and biosafety compared to free StcE. In murine models of colorectal and breast cancer, StcE-nCD47-FNVs significantly suppressed tumor growth and metastasis by remodeling the tumor microenvironment, as evidenced by increased M1 macrophage polarization and CD8 + T cell infiltration. By integrating glycocalyx engineering with vesicle nanotechnology, StcE-nCD47-FNVs offer a safe, robust, and versatile strategy to breach the tumor glycocalyx for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: O-GlcNAc clusters in intrinsically disordered regions regulate transcriptional condensates and gene control
papers.abstract: Abstract Post-translational modifications (PTMs) dynamically regulate the liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) that organizes biomolecular condensates, yet for the monosaccharide O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification, the general rules and their links to protein function remain undefined. Here we identify O-GlcNAc as a widespread LLPS modulator by revealing clustered O-GlcNAc sites enriched in intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) of transcription-related proteins, with bromodomain-containing protein 4 (BRD4) exhibiting this pattern most prominently. Twelve clustered O-GlcNAc sites are identified in BRD4 C-terminal IDR, where modifications decrease condensate size while increasing fluidity in vitro and in cells. Removing O-GlcNAc strengthened BRD4 binding at active enhancers and promoted LLPS-mediated recruitment of transcriptional cofactors, including YTHDC1, leading to elevated expression linked to the cell cycle and DNA repair. Our findings define O-GlcNAc clusters as regulators of condensate material properties and transcriptional outcomes, supporting a general paradigm in which PTMs fine-tune the molecular grammar of biomolecular condensates.

papers.title: Peptide‐Peptide Nucleic Acid Hybrid Hydrogel Based on Sequence Programmable Morphological Change for DNA Data Storage
papers.abstract: Peptide‐based hydrogels provide biocompatible, stimuli‐responsive platforms, while peptide‐DNA hybrids extend programmability through hybridization‐driven crosslinking. However, nucleobase incorporation can influence peptide self‐assembly pathways. We demonstrate that the introduction of bases can directly alter the transition of peptides between gel and solution, offering an alternative mechanism to hybridization‐dependent approaches. Using peptide nucleic acid–guanine as a molecular bridge, guanine attachment shifts peptide assemblies from gel to solution states. Conversely, introducing complementary cytosine‐rich DNA sequences triggers a solution‐to‐gel transition. This morphological switching is sequence‐specific, enabling precise spatiotemporal control of gelation. Structural and rheological analyses confirm guanine's critical role in altering peptide backbone organization and enabling dynamic reconfiguration. As a demonstration of this programmable material's capabilities, we applied the hydrogel for DNA data storage. The hydrogel protects encapsulated DNA information from enzymatic degradation and facilitates precise digital information retrieval, establishing a robust storage medium for synthetic DNA‐encoded data. This strategy leverages nucleic acid sequence specificity to directly manipulate peptide nanostructure, advancing the design of smart, stimuli‐responsive biomaterials.

papers.title: Neutrophil-Inspired Programmable Bacteria for Pyroptosis-Driven Tumor Eradication
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Neutrophils represent a critical component of innate immunity, possessing intrinsic cytotoxic programs involving chemotaxis, degranulation, and lytic effector deployment. Here we report a neutrophil-inspired programmable bacteria (NPB) system developed via synthetic biology and molecular engineering. The nonpathogenic Escherichia coli MG1655 is programmed to execute a sequential four-stage program inspired by the “homing–bursting–lethality” logic of neutrophils with spatiotemporally controlled activation: (I) Preferential homing to hypoxic tumor regions; (II) Sonodynamic actuation of bacterial disruption and on-demand payload release via VHb-mediated ROS generation; (III) Tumor-associated gelatinase-responsive activation of Granzyme B zymogen (m-GzmB-T); and (IV) Pyroptosis-mediated enhancement of systemic antitumor immunity. The NPB system combined with focused ultrasound exhibited consistent antitumor efficacy across murine CT26, MC38, and EMT6 tumor models, while promoting systemic antitumor immune responses and durable immune memory. This work demonstrates the potential of engineering live bacteria with sequential physical and biochemical control mechanisms to execute bioinspired therapeutic cascades, providing a programmable and modular platform for precision cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: A Nano‐Cocoon Platform Attenuates Osteoarthritis Progression via Chem‐Bio Coupled ROS Scavenging and Cartilage Lubrication Restoration
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, cartilage matrix degeneration, and impaired lubrication are central drivers of osteoarthritis (OA). However, poor matrix retention limits drug delivery to chondrocytes and lubrication restoration. Here, we develop a zwitterion‐based, thioketal‐crosslinked Superoxide Dismutase (SOD)‐polymer complex (SOD‐SADT) via in situ atom transfer radical polymerization, in which polymers grow from the enzyme surface and envelop SOD to form a nanoscale cocoon. The polymer shell exhibits cartilage‐matrix affinity through van der Waals and electrostatic interactions with type II collagen and chondroitin sulfate. Accordingly, its zwitterionic hydration layer enables matrix‐anchored lubrication, substantially reducing the coefficient of friction of OA‐like cartilages. Meanwhile, SOD‐SADT establishes a chem‐bio coupling for ROS elimination that couples enzymatic·O 2 − dismutation with thioketal‐triggered chemical depletion of H 2 O 2 and·OH, achieving up to ∼80% ROS scavenging. Notably, SOD‐SADT achieves high chondrocyte uptake (∼ 91.7 ± 3.4%) and promotes lysosomal escape. This enhances intracellular utilization, thereby attenuating oxidative injury and restoring anabolic/catabolic balance. In a mouse model of OA, intra‐articular SOD‐SADT preserves cartilage structure and improves joint function, thereby markedly slowing OA progression. Overall, this work offers a dual‐action strategy that couples intracellular antioxidant regulation with extracellular lubrication repair to address OA.

papers.title: Photoenzymatic Enantioselective [2+2] Cycloaddition of Alkynes Enabled by Whole-Cell Directed Evolution
papers.abstract: Abstract Enantioselective excited-state photocycloadditions represent an attractive yet challenging strategy for accessing optically active strained molecules. Here, we report a whole-cell directed evolution platform for engineering artificial triplet photoenzymes that catalyze the enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition of alkynes. By employing calcium chloride-mediated membrane permeabilization, we overcome substrate accessibility limitations in whole-cell systems and enable high-throughput evolution without the need for cell lysates or purified enzymes. Through ten rounds of directed evolution, a primitive ancestor (APC1.0; 46% yield, 6% ee) was transformed into a highly efficient variant (APC10.0; 92% yield, 94% ee under whole-cell conditions; 99% yield, 97% ee as the purified enzyme). The enhanced activity of APC10.0 enabled a total turnover number of 1800. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for the evolution of artificial photoenzymes and expands the scope of biocatalysis toward stereoselective excited-state transformations.

papers.title: Native Mass Spectrometry-Based Proteoform Explicit Metrics System (PrEMS) Informs Structural Improvement of Artificial Photocyclase Enzymes
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Directed evolution is a powerful strategy for enzyme engineering and has successfully enabled unique stereoselective biosynthesis of high-value organic molecules. Enantiomeric excess (ee) remains the gold standard to assess the enzyme performance, but only reflects the final reaction outcome and provides limited mechanistic insights, leaving design efforts effectively a ″black box″, especially for multimeric proteins and heterogeneous systems. Here, we introduce a Proteoform Explicit Metrics System (PrEMS) that links protein point mutations and catalytic enantioselectivity via structural features measured by native mass spectrometry (native MS). Using 11 artificial photocyclase mutants, we demonstrate that single-point mutations can have a profound impact on protein structure, resulting in a highly convoluted effect on protein function not easily explainable by a single variable. We derived a multiple linear regression (MLR) model from the proteoform explicit native MS data based on the enzyme’s oligomeric state, photosensitizer labeling efficiency, susceptibility to oxidation, and photodegradation half-life. PrEMS showed significantly higher correlation (adjusted R2 increases from 0.053 to 0.869) to the enzyme’s enantioselectivity than the conventional physicochemical descriptors of the mutated amino acids. PrEMS serves as a quantitative framework to fill the knowledge gap in structural descriptors between sequence mutation and the enzyme’s function, rationalizing enzyme improvement strategies. For example, our analysis indicated that photodamage can be suppressed by incorporating aromatic residues near the active site. Our study outlines a tangible path with quantifiable metrics for integrating native MS data into enzyme design workflows.

papers.title: Reprogramming Stereocontrol Through Progressive Substrate Reorganization in Artificial Triplet Photoenzymes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control of stereoselectivity remains a fundamental challenge in artificial enzymatic catalysis, particularly for artificial photoenzymes that lack evolutionary coupling between photosensitizer positioning and substrate recognition. Herein, by integrating crystallography, kinetics, molecular simulations, and protein engineering, we show that the enantioselectivity of an artificial triplet photoenzyme TPe4.0_FBpA for [2+2] cycloaddition originates from a highly organized indole substrate assembly within the photoactive cavity. Guided by these insights, progressive remodeling of substrate organization through minimal active‐site engineering reverses enantiopreference (from 99.5:0.5 e.r. to 2:98 e.r.) while preserving the sequence position of the genetically encoded photosensitizer. Structural and computational analyses further support a switch in the dominant stereocontrol mode from template‐assisted substrate organization to dispersion‐driven conformational confinement. These findings establish substrate organization as a programmable determinant of stereochemical outcome in artificial photoenzymes and provide a mechanistic framework for stereodivergent excited‐state biocatalysis.
